The ADHD treatment population (ADHD-behandlingspopulation) in 2023 is characterized by significant disparities across age groups, gender, and geographic regions. Across all regions, a total of 3,414 patients were registered in ADHD package courses [^src1]. The data reveals that the majority of patients are in the 11–17 years age group, which accounts for 2,134 individuals, making it the leading demographic by a wide margin [^src1]. In contrast, the 0–5 years age group is the smallest, with only 104 patients nationwide [^src1].

Gender distribution shows a clear male dominance across all age brackets, with boys comprising 62% of the total population and girls making up 38% [^src1]. This disparity is most acute in the 6–10 years age group, where boys account for 74% of patients compared to 26% for girls [^src1]. The gap narrows slightly in the 11–17 years group, which is 54% boys and 46% girls [^src1].

Regionally, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] leads with the highest total number of patients at 1,013 [^src1]. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] follows with 841 patients, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] has 647 [^src1]. [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] records 525 patients, and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] has the lowest total with 388 patients [^src1]. A notable outlier in the regional data is [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], which has no registered patients in the 0–5 years age category [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single snapshot from 2023, no longitudinal trends can be established.
